purpose: Identify the independent H2 test oracles and evidence needed for PostgreSQL-backed command/outbox delivery and Temporal execution binding. This matrix is a risk inventory, not an implementation contract, test result, or approval.

scope.direct_slice: H2 database roles, durable command/outbox protocol, Temporal start binding, acknowledgement, projection fencing and recovery; H3/H4 behavior is tested only where required to establish a safe projection boundary.
environments: separately launched API/dispatcher/projector/worker processes where specified

risk_groups.purpose: Prove that each H2 process has only its required database authority and that its login identity is actually authenticated rather than inferred from a caller-controlled session field.
risk_groups.method: Use real PostgreSQL connections under distinct runtime, dispatcher, projector/activity, operator and migration-owner LOGIN roles as fixed by the H2 contract. Verify SCRAM/password authentication from independent processes: each intended credential succeeds; missing and wrong passwords and credentials for another role fail; SET ROLE and role membership do not widen authority. Keep bootstrap/migration-owner access isolated. Exercise both allowed and denied SQL operations, including attempts to change immutable snapshots, job ownership, command identity/payload, outbox state, applied receipt, run binding and projection fields. A separate Temporal-worker DB role is not assumed: one candidate is for Temporal workflow activities to use the narrowly scoped projector credential, but the final authenticated process-to-role mapping must be contractually explicit.
risk_groups.owner: TC authors independent privilege matrix and credential/process harness; main owns migration and process code; independent reviewer audits role grants and proof.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: After H2 contract approval, each role can perform only its enumerated operations; unauthorized operations fail at PostgreSQL; live service connections demonstrate the expected authenticated current_user/session_user. SCRAM evidence is independent of the existing G1 trust-local fixture.
risk_groups.expected_result: Legitimate role operations succeed, denied DML/DDL/role escalation fails, wrong or absent credentials cannot authenticate, and no API/Temporal payload or public evidence contains credentials.
evidence: sanitized process lifecycle and log canary scan
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve database cluster, exact SQL/migration bytes, private credentials and process logs with restricted permissions; classify SQL grant error separately from authentication bypass. Rebuild a fresh isolated cluster after any migration candidate change and rerun H2 plus G1/G4/G5 regression.
unresolved_oracles: Exact role names and operation matrix must be frozen in H2 contract; dispatcher, API runtime, and projector/activity capabilities must be distinguished.

Existing G1 uses trust-local bootstrap/runtime setup; it cannot establish SCRAM authentication for any H2 process. Exact narrow bootstrap exception and whether any existing G1 suite must be rerun under SCRAM remain pending.

A distinct database role for the Temporal worker and projector is not a required assumption. The candidate model is a narrowly scoped projector credential used by Temporal activities, but whether/how that credential is presented and authenticated by the activity process must be fixed in H2 contract.
Exact worker/activity identity binding (Temporal activity info, process authentication, and run_id fence) and cross-check are pending; a payload-supplied worker name is not sufficient evidence.

risk_groups.purpose: Add execution/outbox authority without changing accepted B01/B02 migration bytes or invalidating existing jobs, receipts, workspaces or profile snapshots.
risk_groups.method: Migrate both a fresh database and a database populated by current G4/G5 fixtures. Assert the original create command can be backfilled into the immutable create reference; test duplicate/missing/wrong-route links, foreign keys, uniqueness, nullability, state checks, grants, rerun, drift, rollback and partial migration failure. Exercise allowed human-command linkage without letting it alter the create reference. Use independent SQL expectations derived from the approved contract, not schema introspection as the oracle.
risk_groups.owner: Main owns SQL/migration; TC owns migration and compatibility tests; reviewer checks immutable original migration hashes and SQL authority.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: 001/002 bytes remain exact; migration is deterministic and rerunnable; existing data remains readable; every new constraint/grant matches the approved role matrix; invalid links/duplicate create rows fail atomically.
risk_groups.expected_result: Fresh and upgraded schemas expose the approved execution records, old G4/G5 rows and receipts remain unchanged, and malformed or unauthorized linkage cannot be committed.
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Retain failed cluster and migration bytes, never edit 001/002 to make the upgrade pass. Repair only the new migration, then rerun fresh and populated upgrade paths and all G1/G4/G5 regression suites.
unresolved_oracles: Exact new tables, columns, indexes, constraints, ownership and migration version are pending H2 contract.
Backfill treatment for malformed legacy rows and exact failure code/transaction boundary are pending.
Exact rollback expectations for partially applied PostgreSQL DDL and migration-source drift classification are pending.

risk_groups.purpose: Verify accepted command and outbox creation remain one atomic group and only the immutable create command is joined as the job's origin.
risk_groups.method: Use existing real-PG G4 harness, then observe the approved accepted→dispatched→applied lifecycle. Inject failures around each newly specified insert/link boundary; race same idempotency key and distinct sessions; query list/detail after human commands exist. Probe duplicate create, relink to a human command, payload reinterpretation and foreign-project access.
risk_groups.owner: TC authors HTTP/PG tests and literal expected rows; main owns API and migration; reviewer verifies OpenAPI DTO compatibility.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: The original create receipt is stable; command, job, outbox and workspace-origin invariants are atomic; new commands never duplicate jobs or change create provenance; 202 acceptance is not represented as Temporal dispatch/application.
risk_groups.expected_result: Successful create retains its G4 observable DTO and exact receipt; injected failures leave no partial group; list/detail still return each job once after later command rows are present.
evidence: list/detail query results and create-link constraint probes
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve request ids, private DB state, and fault-boundary logs. Recreate isolated DB per migration candidate; rerun G4 create/idempotency/cross-project races and G5 workspace gating.
unresolved_oracles: Exact accepted command/outbox states, receipt codes and HTTP replay behavior for H2-created commands need the reviewed contract.
Exact atomic transaction hook list and create-command relink database representation are pending.
Whether a create accepted while workspace is not READY remains accepted/pending or receives a specified rejection must be fixed explicitly; READY must never imply execution completion.

risk_groups.purpose: Show one durable delivery owner at a time and ensure expired/stale dispatcher work cannot acknowledge or overwrite a newer attempt.
risk_groups.method: Run at least two independent dispatcher processes against real PostgreSQL. Pause one after claim commit; verify another cannot acquire a live claim; expire/reclaim with the approved database clock; let old and new workers race ack/reject and retry. Include equality-at-expiry, just-before/after expiry, generation boundary/overflow, crash before claim commit and after claim commit.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns process-level barriers and literal row/outcome oracle; main owns dispatcher/claim implementation; reviewer checks fencing and database lock ordering.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: Exactly one current lease may mutate delivery state; stale token/generation outcomes change no row, command receipt, job projection or Temporal binding. Claims are committed before external RPC and network waits do not hold PG row locks.
risk_groups.expected_result: At-least-once delivery attempts may occur, but only a current claim can record the definitive result and duplicate attempts resolve against the same deterministic workflow identity.
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Keep exact DB snapshot and both process logs; stop only the owned process handles; classify lock timeout versus stale-fence defect. Re-run claim, crash and concurrency cases on a clean cluster.
unresolved_oracles: Lease duration, retry schedule, attempt numbering, claim eligibility and stale outcome codes are not yet an H2 contract.
Whether dispatch rejection is retryable, terminal or operator-visible depends on the approved error taxonomy.
Exact fencing columns and the source of authoritative database time are pending.

risk_groups.purpose: Prove AT-16 delivery across each PostgreSQL/Temporal durability cut: accepted command is not lost and the same command does not create a second effective workflow execution.
risk_groups.method: With real PG and persistent local Temporal, kill/restart API and dispatcher at: before API commit; after command/outbox commit before claim; after claim commit before RPC; while start response is delayed; after Temporal accepted start but before local ack; after ack before projection; after projection commit before activity response. Restart fresh process instances and replay the same immutable command_id. Assert exact Temporal workflow ID and history, PostgreSQL attempt/ack rows and business transition count after each recovery.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns fault barriers, actual process kill/restart and independent receipt/history oracle; main owns API/dispatcher/workflow/activity; reviewer audits crash boundary coverage.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: A committed accepted command remains recoverable; an uncommitted command has no durable partial group; start-response uncertainty is reconciled against exact workflow identity; there is one effective business execution and no job transition based solely on 202 or outbox dispatched.
risk_groups.expected_result: Precommit failures leave no accepted group; postcommit failures are redelivered/reconciled by the same command/workflow identity; duplicate Temporal start attempts do not duplicate effective projection; projected receipt is durable and replayable.
evidence: process lifecycle identities and kill points
Temporal workflow ID/run ID/history before and after restart
private logs/canary scan and source bundle
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve both PG and Temporal persistent stores before cleanup, all worker/dispatcher logs, and exact fault index. Do not reset Temporal history to hide duplicates. Re-run the failed cut point and then the full H2 crash matrix; retain G4/G5 regression evidence.
unresolved_oracles: Exact ordering and durable meaning of accepted/dispatched/applied, including which transitions write each field, require H2 contract.
Exact deterministic Temporal ID/type/queue/build binding fields and uniqueness constraints require contract.
Fault injection mechanism must interrupt real separate processes at the durable cut; in-process exceptions alone are insufficient acceptance evidence.

risk_groups.purpose: Prevent blind restart when Temporal start outcome is unknown and prevent recreating a workflow when prior history is absent or retention is unverified.
risk_groups.method: Use a real Temporal server with controlled response loss after acceptance, unavailable server before acceptance, delayed visibility, exact-ID NotFound inside the approved window, expired window, unverified namespace retention and a known run whose history is unavailable. Verify the bounded retry policy uses the same workflow ID and command binding, and assert no fallback UUID/ID reuse. Include restart during every reconciliation decision.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns persistent-server behavior and literal bounded window cases; main owns reconciliation state machine; reviewer validates no unsafe re-create path.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: Only a contract-authorized, finite reconciliation path may retry the same start; unknown/expired/unverified cases remain isolated for operator action. A known prior run with missing history is never recreated.
risk_groups.expected_result: Safe deterministic observation can resolve an accepted start; all ambiguous or unsafe cases stay RECONCILING without second semantic execution or changed binding.
evidence: Temporal retention configuration and query results
assertion that alternate ID and reuse were not attempted
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Retain Temporal DB/history and PG binding. Do not erase a workflow to restore green status. Re-run the exact reconciliation branch on a new isolated namespace/database after correcting implementation.
unresolved_oracles: The plan bounds reconciliation to at most one hour and below verified namespace retention, but exact duration, polling/backoff, NotFound visibility grace and state/error codes remain pending.
Exact signal for retention verification and known-history-missing detection need H2 contract.

Physical Temporal history deletion/retention-expiry simulation may not be safely reproducible locally; contract must specify an explicit deterministic test seam or record this limit without claiming coverage.

risk_groups.purpose: Ensure dispatched, applied, workflow progress and PostgreSQL projection are distinct facts, and that duplicate/stale activity results cannot advance current business state.
risk_groups.method: Drive the synthetic pinned workflow through accepted start and an approved transition. Inject activity retries after PG commit-before-response, duplicate same key/same digest, same key/different digest, old revision, old transition sequence, old run_id, stale cycle/attempt, out-of-order event and crash between projection and next workflow action. Read both Temporal history and PG rows after restart.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns independent transition oracle/history assertions; main owns Temporal workflow/activity and PG projector; reviewer audits single-writer/fence.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: Same identity and same payload returns the original immutable receipt; conflicting digest is quarantined; stale execution/revision/sequence has no business effect; workflow does not advance to the next business action before projection outcome is durable.
risk_groups.expected_result: Each accepted business transition has one effective projection and one stable receipt; Temporal activity replays are idempotent; `dispatched` remains nonterminal until projection records applied/rejected.
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve history and DB snapshot; never manually edit projection to match workflow. Correct the idempotency/fencing boundary, then rerun the same transition/replay matrix plus G4 command and G5 workspace tests.
unresolved_oracles: Exact receipt schema, transition sequence allocation, digest inputs, terminal codes and transaction lock order are pending H2/H3 contract.
Exact activity retry behavior and whether projection conflict becomes workflow failure or RECONCILING must be specified.
The exact division between Temporal authoritative state and PostgreSQL query projection needs a reviewed field-by-field mapping.

risk_groups.purpose: Keep user-facing API authorization distinct from internal projection idempotency: external command/job reads require current authentication and access, while an authenticated and statically scoped projector may replay an already committed exact transition receipt without reevaluating mutable human authority.
risk_groups.method: Run two explicitly separate paths. (1) External API: accept a command, then revoke/expire the session or membership and repeat the HTTP request/read; assert the current 401/403 denial and no receipt disclosure, preserving the existing G4 ordering in jobs.py where current authentication, membership and ownership checks precede receipt return. A still-authorized exact retry must return its original receipt; changed body/key and stale/foreign scope must not mutate state. (2) Internal projection: under an authenticated machine/activity principal and validated static project/job/run scope, inject a retry of the same already-committed (job_id, transition_sequence, digest) and assert the immutable stored receipt is returned before rechecking mutable human membership/eligibility; on the first apply, assert current human authority is checked and revocation prevents mutation. Race revocation against first apply using the approved lock order.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns real-PG/API independent session tests; main owns auth/command application; reviewer checks authority-versus-replay ordering.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: External API behavior preserves current G4 auth-before-receipt checks: revoked/expired/unauthorized clients cannot retrieve a receipt. For internal projection only, an authenticated machine principal with valid static scope can replay an exact already-committed receipt without changing it; the first application requires current human authority; conflicting digest or stale run/revision has no business effect.
risk_groups.expected_result: The two receipt paths remain distinct: authorized exact API retries are stable, unauthorized external retries are denied, and internal activity retries are idempotent only after machine identity and static scope are validated.
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Retain private auth/session/DB evidence; use fresh isolated users/projects for each rerun. Re-run G4 auth and job regressions after any authority-lock change.
unresolved_oracles: Exact H2/H4 command-specific external API status codes and immutable receipt identity are pending contract; current G4 401/403 denial after session/membership revocation must remain authoritative and must not disclose the old receipt.

Exact internal projection receipt lookup key/digest, static project/job/run scope, machine-principal authentication, and whether a previously accepted command can be applied after human authority changes must be fixed. Receipt-first replay is allowed only within this internal scoped path; do not transfer that ordering to user-facing API handlers.
Project-guard/job/task/outbox/execution-binding lock order and concurrency result are pending H2/H4 contract.

risk_groups.purpose: Guard only the H2 activation boundary around pending human commands; full P07/P21 human workflow, notifications and route acceptance belong to later H3/H4 contracts and tests.
target: H2 command/outbox acceptance for a human route
risk_groups.method: In H2, verify that a human-command request can only be accepted or rejected according to the approved command contract, that its inbox/outbox linkage is durable and scoped, and that agent completion or workspace READY alone cannot consume a human task or mark the workflow applied. Do not run or claim the full P07/P21 route scenario at this stage. Reserve task creation, durable human wait/restart, supported outcome mapping and notifications for H3/H4 tests.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns H2 boundary tests and later separately reviewed H3/H4 human-flow tests; main owns command/workflow integration; reviewer checks the phase boundary.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: H2 activation does not turn accepted human commands into applied state and does not advance a human-gated workflow without the later validated human transition. Workspace READY and agent `completed` do not imply step success.
risk_groups.expected_result: H2 proves only the durable/non-advancing command boundary; full AT-05 and P07/P21 outcome routing remain deferred and unaccepted until H3/H4.
evidence: before/after job revision and transition receipt
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve human task, command receipt and history. Re-run G4 auth/job tests, G5 workspace gate and H2 delivery cases after fixing task/application ordering.
unresolved_oracles: P07/P21 task creation, outcome mapping, task expiry, notification dedupe, signals and error/status mapping are deferred to reviewed H3/H4 contracts; none is an H2 acceptance oracle.
AT-05 full scenario is deferred, not established by an H2 accepted-command row. Artifact references remain synthetic until B04 upload.
Whether H2 persists a human command without creating the task, and the exact task/notification insertion transaction and retry identity, must be decided in H2/H3/H4 contracts.

risk_groups.purpose: Check H2 start-binding rejects incompatible/missing build identity and records immutable workflow-definition metadata; full v1 wait/v2 deployment/resume acceptance is deferred to H5.
risk_groups.method: For H2, start only the approved synthetic current-version workflow and probe missing/unknown/mismatched build, snapshot and command bindings, plus attempted ID reuse/fallback. Assert fail-closed behavior and immutable binding. Do not claim H2 has run a v1 human-wait/v2 rollout scenario. H5 will later run real pinned v1 history across a separate v2 worker deployment and compatible v1 resume.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns H2 immutable-binding probes and later separate H5 two-build lifecycle tests; main owns registration/worker deployment; reviewer checks phase scope and binding immutability.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: H2 rejects unknown or mismatched execution identity and prevents alternate ID/reuse. Full old-history compatibility and resumption are not H2 pass criteria.
risk_groups.expected_result: H2 produces only binding-level evidence; AT-29 remains deferred to H5 and is not inferred from current-version replay.
evidence: v1/v2 source, environment, task-queue and bundle hashes
worker process identity and poll/route outcomes
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Keep both builds and retained history. Do not reset/recreate old workflows. Restore the compatible worker only for diagnosis, then fix version pinning and repeat H2 start-binding plus AT-29 cases.
unresolved_oracles: Exact Temporal worker versioning API, build ID/task queue format, bundle hash contents, and retention/retirement policy are pending approved H2 contract.
The plan prohibits continue-as-new/workflow retry replacing a pinned run; any future exception requires a separately reviewed handoff contract.
Full v1 human-wait/v2 deployment/v1 resume and original AT-29 acceptance are explicitly deferred to H5; no H2 binding probe substitutes for that scenario.

risk_groups.purpose: Ensure B03 does not regress the accepted G4 API/auth/receipt rules or G5 READY workspace isolation, and does not expose secrets in Temporal payload/history or evidence.
target: existing 001/002 schemas and all G4/G5 tests
Temporal history, task payloads and logs
risk_groups.method: Run pinned G1/G2/G3/G4/G5 suites on the H2 candidate. Assert workspace READY remains separate from command dispatch/application; accepted G4 create receipt and cross-project protections remain unchanged. Seed private canary values in synthetic passwords, DSNs, OAuth/session values, comments and profile text; scan service stdout/stderr, Temporal history, DTOs, audit records and public evidence for raw values.
risk_groups.owner: TC owns immutable regression inventory and canary assertions; main owns integrated runner; independent reviewer audits evidence minimization.
risk_groups.pass_criteria: All required prior suites pass with exact inventory and zero skip; original migrations remain byte-identical; private canaries are absent from public/Temporal workflow payloads and logs; no server-side behavior claims exceed local tested scope.
risk_groups.expected_result: Existing G4/G5 observable behavior and protection boundaries remain intact while new execution fields are separately validated; only sanitized identifiers/counts/hashes are published.
evidence: private log hashes/permissions and canary-scan summary
risk_groups.failure_recovery: Preserve failing candidate bundle, raw private logs and DB/workspace state; diagnose the changed boundary, repair, then rerun affected G4/G5 groups and the full frozen regression gate.
unresolved_oracles: Exact required final suite inventory and source/output pin set must be frozen in H2 runner contract.
No current test proves any Temporal runtime or activity because B03 is not implemented in current local service.
Original AT-05/16/29 and production/SSO/environment acceptance remain unexecuted until their full endpoint scenario and separate deployment environment are run.

contract_gaps_before_H2_authoring: Freeze exact H2 migration tables/columns/constraints/backfill and byte-preservation checks for migrations 001/002.

Freeze distinct SCRAM-authenticated LOGIN roles, credential provisioning, DB operation matrix, process identity proof, SET ROLE/membership denial and narrow bootstrap exception; do not reuse G1 trust-local authentication as evidence.
Freeze immutable command/outbox/attempt/execution-binding schemas, status transitions, claim lease/fencing, retry/backoff, poison/error mapping and HTTP receipt semantics.

Freeze deterministic Temporal workflow ID/type/task queue/build/snapshot/bundle binding fields, no-reuse behavior, exact unknown-start reconciliation duration/poll policy and retention verification oracle.
Freeze applied projection/transition identity, digest inputs, lock order, receipt transaction and activity retry/conflict semantics.
Provide process-level deterministic crash barriers for every PostgreSQL commit / Temporal RPC / acknowledgement / projection cut point and evidence layout with owned-process cleanup.
Specify whether physical history-missing or retention-expiry cases use a supported local test seam; do not simulate them by mutating unrelated production state or claim untested coverage.
